notes: Token ids and names come from the AtlasLoot parse (vendor/atlasloot/data-tbc.lua row comments); zone and boss from data/atlasloot_sources.json keyed on the TOKEN id. The TBC tier tokens do not appear in db.json at all, so no classAllowlist or tooltip witnesses their class grouping.

Set piece ids come from db.json by `setId`, and the piece-to-token pairing is a SLOT JOIN on db.json's `type` field, not a witnessed redemption list. No committed input states which token buys which piece. The join reproduces both committed files (ret 18 entries, feral 15) exactly, which is a consistency check rather than an independent one.

T4/T5 group: Defender. T6 group: Conqueror. The T6 vocabulary is Conqueror/Vanquisher/Protector and the class triples are RE-CUT, not renamed -- paladin goes Champion->Conqueror but druid goes Defender->Vanquisher. See data/two-hop/feral-tokens.json notes 9-10, which record that 'druid uses the Defender-equivalent' would have been wrong.

The class triples are witnessed by committed data, not by elimination: each tier piece's `classAllowlist` in vendor/wowsims/db.json names the one class that can wear it (decode against data/proto/common.proto:96-104 -- 3 Hunter, 8 Mage, 9 Warlock, and so on), so grouping the pieces a token buys yields its triple directly. Champion = Paladin/Rogue/Shaman, Defender = Druid/Priest/Warrior, Hero = Hunter/Mage/Warlock at T4 and T5; at T6 the vocabulary changes to Conqueror/Vanquisher/Protector AND the triples are re-cut -- Vanquisher = Rogue/Mage/Druid, Protector = Warrior/Hunter/Shaman, Conqueror = Paladin/Priest/Warlock. Re-derive with: python -c "import json,glob;from collections import defaultdict;db=json.load(open('vendor/wowsims/db.json'));byid={int(i['id']):i for i in db['items']};t=defaultdict(set);[t[e['tokenName']].add(c) for f in glob.glob('data/two-hop/*-tokens.json') for e in json.load(open(f))['entries'] for c in (byid.get(e['pieceId'],{}).get('classAllowlist') or [])];print({k:sorted(v) for k,v in sorted(t.items())})". An earlier version of this note called the T4/T5 Hero column unwitnessed; that was wrong -- it was derived by elimination when the allowlist was there all along.
